issue.title: test_no_system_clock_display_sites fails: completion/candidates/catalog_plans.py reads the process clock directly (482fb46bc)
issue.description:
`tests/test_timezone_display_guard.py::test_no_system_clock_display_sites` is red on master
(observed by the sase-17p land agent at 682089c84, 2026-09-24, in `just test-scoped`).
Beside a Command Line hit already routed to active epic sase-17x (block_render.py:105),
it flags bare process-clock calls added by 482fb46bc "feat(completion): TAB completion for
pending plan names" (sase-17z.2; epic sase-17z is closed, so this cannot be a DISCOVERED
ISSUE note on it):

- src/sase/completion/candidates/catalog_plans.py:380
  `int((datetime.now().astimezone() - parsed).total_seconds())`
- catalog_plans.py:403 `parsed.replace(tzinfo=datetime.now().astimezone().tzinfo)`
- catalog_plans.py:410 `tzinfo=datetime.now().astimezone().tzinfo`

Root cause: the pending-plan age/description helper reads the system clock and timezone
directly instead of through `sase.core.time` (the guard's docstring: "Fix new hits by
routing through sase.core.time before extending the allowlist"). Remedy: use the
sase.core.time now/timezone helpers for the relative-age computation and the naive-time
tzinfo fallback; do not extend `_ALLOWED_CLOCK_DISPLAY_SITES`.

Not caused by epic sase-17p (its diff touches no completion candidate provider).

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic static AST guard over src/sase: it reports the same three catalog_plans.py call sites on every run; no timing or environment dependence.
